AI.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAI applications fail without shared context. LLMs are powerful, but without a structured, unified context layer — one that bridges silos, captures complex relationships, and enforces governance — agents hallucinate, violate policies, and produce non-deterministic outcomes.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTrustGraph builds that layer. It uses hypergraphs to turn raw enterprise data into AI-ready context: a unified semantic context layer where agentic outcomes are deterministic and agent behavior is not just traceable, but cryptographically verifiable.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe Problem: \"Common Context Understanding\"\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-the-problem-common-context-understanding\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: The Problem: \u0026quot;Common Context Understanding\u0026quot;\" href=\"#the-problem-common-context-understanding\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTo understand why AI struggles in the enterprise, consider Abbott and Costello’s classic \u003ca href=\"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sYOUFGfK4bU\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003e\"Who's on First?\"\u003c/a\u003e routine.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAbbott explains the baseball lineup: \u003ccode\u003eWho\u003c/code\u003e is on first base, \u003ccode\u003eWhat\u003c/code\u003e is on second base, and \u003ccode\u003eI Don't Know\u003c/code\u003e is on third base. Costello is driven mad because he assumes Abbott is asking questions rather than stating the names of the players: \u003ccode\u003eWho\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eWhat\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003eI Don't Know\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTwo agents cannot communicate if they do not share the same context understanding.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv similarity, it breaks completely.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIf a user asks: \"\u003cem\u003eWho is playing on first base?\u003c/em\u003e\"\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThe vector database converts the query into an embedding.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eSemantic similarity searches for vectors close to \"playing,\" \"first base,\" and \"who.\"\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eBecause \"Who\" is a common pronoun, the embedding space maps it to general inquiries about identity, not the specific name of a baseball player.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThe LLM retrieves irrelevant documents and hallucinates, failing to understand that \"Who\" is an entity (a Person), not a question.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSemantic similarity operates on fuzzy, statistical probability. It cannot distinguish between the linguistic usage of a word as a pronoun and its usage as a proper noun within a specific, localized context.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhy HyperGraphs Solve Context\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-why-hypergraphs-solve-context\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Why HyperGraphs Solve Context\" href=\"#why-hypergraphs-solve-context\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA HyperGraph, specifically built using standards like RDF and OWL, establishes explicit, unambiguous semantics. It doesn't rely on \"guessing\" based on word proximity; it relies on defined relationships.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eHere is the \"Who's on First\" routine modeled in RDF with an OWL ontology. .\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhen an agent queries a TrustGraph hypergraph, it uses SPARQL or GraphRAG to traverse these explicit paths. The agent knows that \u003ccode\u003e:Who\u003c/code\u003e is a \u003ccode\u003e:Player\u003c/code\u003e whose \u003ccode\u003e:playsPosition\u003c/code\u003e is \u003ccode\u003e:FirstBase\u003c/code\u003e. Hallucination is eliminated because context is structured, not inferred via probability.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eGoing Beyond Traditional Graphs: The Hypergraph\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-going-beyond-traditional-graphs-the-hypergraph\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Going Beyond Traditional Graphs: The Hypergraph\" href=\"#going-beyond-traditional-graphs-the-hypergraph\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eStandard Knowledge Graphs (KGs) are limited to binary relationships (Node A → Node B). Enterprise context is rarely this simple.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTrustGraph leverages \u003ca href=\"https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf12-concepts/\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eRDF 1.2\u003c/a\u003e and \u003ca href=\"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Named_graph\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eNamed Graphs\u003c/a\u003e as \u003ca href=\"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N-Triples#N-Quads\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eN-Quads\u003c/a\u003e to achieve a cutting-edge hypergraph architecture. RDF 1.2 introduces the ability to reference entire statements (triples) as nodes themselves. Combining RDF 1.2 with Named Graphs enbables grouping complex, multi-entity events into a single, addressable conceptual unit for true n-ary relationships.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eStandard Knowledge Graph: \u003ccode\u003eDocument\u003c/code\u003e → \u003ccode\u003eAuthor\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eTrustGraph Hypergraph: Connects \u003ccode\u003eDocument\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eAuthor\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eApproving Manager\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eCompliance Policy\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003eTime/Location\u003c/code\u003e Metadata into a single, complex relational event.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eBYOO: TrustGraph allows you to \u003cstrong\u003eBring-Your-Own-Ontology\u003c/strong\u003e which can be loaded in \u003ca href=\"https://www.w3.org/TR/owl2-rdf-based-semantics/\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eOWL\u003c/a\u003e format. The ontology-enabled hypergraph will use the provided ontology for semantic compliance for all ingested data, dramatically improving agentic accuracy and precision. Ontology-compliant retrieval is automated.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis hyper-relational context is what enables autonomous agents to reason through complex enterprise workflows and governance policies.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eCore Capabilities of the Interoperability Layer\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-core-capabilities-of-the-interoperability-layer\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Core Capabilities of the Interoperability Layer\" href=\"#core-capabilities-of-the-interoperability-layer\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTrustGraph provides the infrastructure to convert raw data into agentic context and manage it at scale.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eRaw Data to AI-Ready Context\nTrustGraph isn't just a graph database; it is a processing engine. It ingests unstructured, raw enterprise data (PDFs, wikis, APIs, databases), extracts entities and relationships using LLMs, and structures them directly into the hypergraph—transforming chaotic data into AI-ready context.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eHyperflows: Custom Agents and Workloads\nHyperflows are unique agentic workflows where processing capabilities are chained together. Developers can configure specific LLMs and specific Context Graph access permissions for every step of a workflow. A Hyperflow can route a query from a lightweight local model for classification, to a heavy reasoning model, drawing from different hypergraph collections at each step based on governance rules.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eContext Management: Workspaces, Collections, and Context Cores\nManaging enterprise context requires strict orchestration. TrustGraph provides purpose-built context management features:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eWorkspaces: Deep, programmatic data isolation for users, agents, and hyperflows. Ensure that an HR agent cannot read financial data, and multi-tenant data remains strictly compartmentalized.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eCollections: Enterprise knowledge bases aren't just flat files. Manage, partition, and query distinct knowledge bases directly within the hypergraph. Dynamically combine a \"Product Specs\" collection and a \"Support Tickets\" collection in real-time for an agent.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eContext Cores: Modular, portable, and reusable units of context. Package domain-specific knowledge into a Context Core and plug it into any agent or workflow. <div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The Context Orchestration Layer for Agentic AI</h3><a id="user-content-the-context-orchestration-layer-for-agentic-ai" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The Context Orchestration Layer for Agentic AI" href="#the-context-orchestration-layer-for-agentic-ai"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://trendshift.io/repositories/17291" rel="nofollow"><img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/b3269ad98d5ccd5f25198732899bfcdbfa967ae75ae94212cd30cd80e30731f3/68747470733a2f2f7472656e6473686966742e696f2f6170692f62616467652f7265706f7369746f726965732f3137323931" alt="trustgraph-ai%2Ftrustgraph | Trendshift" style="width: 250px; height: 55px; max-width: 100%;; aspect-ratio: 250 / 55; background-color: var(--bgColor-muted); border-radius: 6px" width="250" height="55" data-canonical-src="https://trendshift.io/api/badge/repositories/17291" class="js-gh-image-fallback"></a></p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Open Source · Open Standards · Total Transparency</strong></p>
</div>
<hr>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://trustgraph.ai" rel="nofollow">TrustGraph</a> is an open-source context orchestration layer designed to power the next generation of enterprise AI.</p>
<p dir="auto">AI applications fail without shared context. LLMs are powerful, but without a structured, unified context layer — one that bridges silos, captures complex relationships, and enforces governance — agents hallucinate, violate policies, and produce non-deterministic outcomes.</p>
<p dir="auto">TrustGraph builds that layer. It uses hypergraphs to turn raw enterprise data into AI-ready context: a unified semantic context layer where agentic outcomes are deterministic and agent behavior is not just traceable, but cryptographically verifiable.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The Problem: "Common Context Understanding"</h2><a id="user-content-the-problem-common-context-understanding" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The Problem: "Common Context Understanding"" href="#the-problem-common-context-understanding"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">To understand why AI struggles in the enterprise, consider Abbott and Costello’s classic <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sYOUFGfK4bU" rel="nofollow">"Who's on First?"</a> routine.</p>
<p dir="auto">Abbott explains the baseball lineup: <code>Who</code> is on first base, <code>What</code> is on second base, and <code>I Don't Know</code> is on third base. Costello is driven mad because he assumes Abbott is asking questions rather than stating the names of the players: <code>Who</code>, <code>What</code>, and <code>I Don't Know</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Two agents cannot communicate if they do not share the same context understanding.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why Vector Embeddings and Semantic Search Fail Here</h2><a id="user-content-why-vector-embeddings-and-semantic-search-fail-here" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why Vector Embeddings and Semantic Search Fail Here" href="#why-vector-embeddings-and-semantic-search-fail-here"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">If you feed this scenario into a standard RAG pipeline using vector embeddings and semantic similarity, it breaks completely.</p>
<p dir="auto">If a user asks: "<em>Who is playing on first base?</em>"</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>The vector database converts the query into an embedding.</li>
<li>Semantic similarity searches for vectors close to "playing," "first base," and "who."</li>
<li>Because "Who" is a common pronoun, the embedding space maps it to general inquiries about identity, not the specific name of a baseball player.</li>
<li>The LLM retrieves irrelevant documents and hallucinates, failing to understand that "Who" is an entity (a Person), not a question.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Semantic similarity operates on fuzzy, statistical probability. It cannot distinguish between the linguistic usage of a word as a pronoun and its usage as a proper noun within a specific, localized context.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why HyperGraphs Solve Context</h2><a id="user-content-why-hypergraphs-solve-context" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why HyperGraphs Solve Context" href="#why-hypergraphs-solve-context"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">A HyperGraph, specifically built using standards like RDF and OWL, establishes explicit, unambiguous semantics. It doesn't rely on "guessing" based on word proximity; it relies on defined relationships.</p>
<p dir="auto">Here is the "Who's on First" routine modeled in RDF with an OWL ontology. By structuring data this way, the LLM knows exactly what "Who" means in this context:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-turtle notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="@prefix : <http://trustgraph.ai/baseball#> .
@prefix rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#> .
@prefix rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .
@prefix owl: <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#> .

# Ontology Classes
:Player a owl:Class ;
    rdfs:subClassOf owl:Thing .

:BaseballPosition a owl:Class .

# Object Properties
:playsPosition a owl:ObjectProperty ;
    rdfs:domain :Player ;
    rdfs:range :BaseballPosition .

# Data (The Context)
:Who a :Player ;
    rdfs:label "Who" .

:What a :Player ;
    rdfs:label "What" .

:IDontKnow a :Player ;
    rdfs:label "I Don't Know" .

:FirstBase a :BaseballPosition ;
    rdfs:label "First Base" .

:SecondBase a :BaseballPosition ;
    rdfs:label "Second Base" .

:ThirdBase a :BaseballPosition ;
    rdfs:label "Third Base" .

# The Explicit Relationships
:Who :playsPosition :FirstBase .
:What :playsPosition :SecondBase .
:IDontKnow :playsPosition :ThirdBase ."><pre><span class="pl-k">@prefix</span> : <span class="pl-en"><http://trustgraph.ai/baseball#></span> .
<span class="pl-k">@prefix</span> rdf: <span class="pl-en"><http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#></span> .
<span class="pl-k">@prefix</span> rdfs: <span class="pl-en"><http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#></span> .
<span class="pl-k">@prefix</span> owl: <span class="pl-en"><http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#></span> .

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Ontology Classes</span>
:Player <span class="pl-k">a</span> owl:Class ;
    rdfs:subClassOf owl:Thing .

:BaseballPosition <span class="pl-k">a</span> owl:Class .

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Object Properties</span>
:playsPosition <span class="pl-k">a</span> owl:ObjectProperty ;
    rdfs:domain :Player ;
    rdfs:range :BaseballPosition .

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Data (The Context)</span>
:Who <span class="pl-k">a</span> :Player ;
    rdfs:label <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Who<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> .

:What <span class="pl-k">a</span> :Player ;
    rdfs:label <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>What<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> .

:IDontKnow <span class="pl-k">a</span> :Player ;
    rdfs:label <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>I Don't Know<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> .

:FirstBase <span class="pl-k">a</span> :BaseballPosition ;
    rdfs:label <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>First Base<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> .

:SecondBase <span class="pl-k">a</span> :BaseballPosition ;
    rdfs:label <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Second Base<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> .

:ThirdBase <span class="pl-k">a</span> :BaseballPosition ;
    rdfs:label <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Third Base<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> .

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> The Explicit Relationships</span>
:Who :playsPosition :FirstBase .
:What :playsPosition :SecondBase .
:IDontKnow :playsPosition :ThirdBase .</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">When an agent queries a TrustGraph hypergraph, it uses SPARQL or GraphRAG to traverse these explicit paths. The agent knows that <code>:Who</code> is a <code>:Player</code> whose <code>:playsPosition</code> is <code>:FirstBase</code>. Hallucination is eliminated because context is structured, not inferred via probability.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Going Beyond Traditional Graphs: The Hypergraph</h2><a id="user-content-going-beyond-traditional-graphs-the-hypergraph" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Going Beyond Traditional Graphs: The Hypergraph" href="#going-beyond-traditional-graphs-the-hypergraph"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Standard Knowledge Graphs (KGs) are limited to binary relationships (Node A → Node B). Enterprise context is rarely this simple.</p>
<p dir="auto">TrustGraph leverages <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf12-concepts/" rel="nofollow">RDF 1.2</a> and <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Named_graph" rel="nofollow">Named Graphs</a> as <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N-Triples#N-Quads" rel="nofollow">N-Quads</a> to achieve a cutting-edge hypergraph architecture. RDF 1.2 introduces the ability to reference entire statements (triples) as nodes themselves. Combining RDF 1.2 with Named Graphs enbables grouping complex, multi-entity events into a single, addressable conceptual unit for true n-ary relationships.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Standard Knowledge Graph: <code>Document</code> → <code>Author</code></li>
<li>TrustGraph Hypergraph: Connects <code>Document</code>, <code>Author</code>, <code>Approving Manager</code>, <code>Compliance Policy</code>, and <code>Time/Location</code> Metadata into a single, complex relational event.</li>
<li>BYOO: TrustGraph allows you to <strong>Bring-Your-Own-Ontology</strong> which can be loaded in <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/owl2-rdf-based-semantics/" rel="nofollow">OWL</a> format. The ontology-enabled hypergraph will use the provided ontology for semantic compliance for all ingested data, dramatically improving agentic accuracy and precision. Ontology-compliant retrieval is automated.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">This hyper-relational context is what enables autonomous agents to reason through complex enterprise workflows and governance policies.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Core Capabilities of the Interoperability Layer</h2><a id="user-content-core-capabilities-of-the-interoperability-layer" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Core Capabilities of the Interoperability Layer" href="#core-capabilities-of-the-interoperability-layer"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">TrustGraph provides the infrastructure to convert raw data into agentic context and manage it at scale.</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto">Raw Data to AI-Ready Context
TrustGraph isn't just a graph database; it is a processing engine. It ingests unstructured, raw enterprise data (PDFs, wikis, APIs, databases), extracts entities and relationships using LLMs, and structures them directly into the hypergraph—transforming chaotic data into AI-ready context.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto">Hyperflows: Custom Agents and Workloads
Hyperflows are unique agentic workflows where processing capabilities are chained together. Developers can configure specific LLMs and specific Context Graph access permissions for every step of a workflow. A Hyperflow can route a query from a lightweight local model for classification, to a heavy reasoning model, drawing from different hypergraph collections at each step based on governance rules.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto">Context Management: Workspaces, Collections, and Context Cores
Managing enterprise context requires strict orchestration. TrustGraph provides purpose-built context management features:</p>
</li>
</ol>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Workspaces: Deep, programmatic data isolation for users, agents, and hyperflows. Ensure that an HR agent cannot read financial data, and multi-tenant data remains strictly compartmentalized.</li>
<li>Collections: Enterprise knowledge bases aren't just flat files. Manage, partition, and query distinct knowledge bases directly within the hypergraph. Dynamically combine a "Product Specs" collection and a "Support Tickets" collection in real-time for an agent.</li>
<li>Context Cores: Modular, portable, and reusable units of context. Package domain-specific knowledge into a Context Core and plug it into any agent or workflow. It’s context-as-a-service.</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">Beyond the hypergraph and context management, TrustGraph is built to provide the full agentic stack for enterprise AI.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Provenance (Real-Time Traceability): TrustGraph captures all event metadata in the hypergraph, providing real-time traceability for every decision an agent makes. If an agent takes an action, you can trace the exact path through the hypergraph that led to that outcome—solving the "black box" problem for enterprise compliance.</li>
<li>Open LLM Inference Stack: Don't lock your enterprise data behind proprietary API paywalls. TrustGraph includes a built-in LLM inference stack capable of running open-source models on any hardware (Nvidia, AMD, or Intel accelerators), keeping your data and compute entirely within your sovereignty.</li>
<li>Deployment Flexibility: Enterprise requirements dictate where data lives. TrustGraph can be totally self-hosted (air-gapped on-premise), deployed as Bring-Your-Own-Cloud (BYOC) into your existing VPC, or consumed as a fully managed SaaS.</li>
</ul>
